_about: The player's race shop: haulers, shop facilities and team (owner mode) facilities. Money in 2025 USD. Prices are midpoints of researched ranges (docs/research/race_shop_economics.md); effects are game-design values (EST) unless a note says otherwise.

haulers.label: Open car trailer
haulers.about: An 18-20 ft open steel trailer behind the family pickup. Cheap to tow; the car rides in the weather and the spares ride in the truck bed.
haulers.note: 18 ft open trailer $4,300-7,200 new (2025-26 dealer listings, high); towed with the family pickup.

haulers.label: Enclosed trailer (24 ft)
haulers.about: A 24 ft enclosed trailer: room for a tire rack, a toolbox and the spare parts you'd otherwise leave at home. Sides that carry a sponsor's name.
haulers.note: 24 ft enclosed $11,000-22,000 new (2024-26, medium); trailer + contents insurance $1,000-1,500/yr (medium).

haulers.label: Race trailer & dually (32 ft)
haulers.about: A 32 ft gooseneck race trailer with cabinets, a generator, an awning and a lounge, pulled by a one-ton dually. The touring racer's rig.
haulers.note: EST: a gooseneck race trailer ($60-95k new for a 48 ft, 2025) bought used, plus a used one-ton dually (new 3/4-ton diesel from ~$58k, 2025).

haulers.label: Stacker trailer & truck
haulers.about: A 48 ft stacker with a hydraulic lift: two cars, a full parts shop and a tire bay, behind a medium-duty truck. The backup car comes to every race.
haulers.note: 28 ft stacker with lift $105-128k new (2024-26, medium) plus a truck; a toter + stacker 'mobile race shop' $150-250k (2017, medium).

haulers.label: Semi transporter
haulers.about: A used tractor and a 53 ft race transporter: two cars upstairs, a machine shop downstairs and a lounge up front. Needs a CDL driver. Sponsors notice.
haulers.note: Used semi rig ~$250k at dirt late model / modified level (2017) and $300-350k at Xfinity (2025), medium; ~$0.82/mi running before driver pay (EST from ATRI). Upkeep includes a part-time CDL driver (EST).

space.label: Shop space

levels.label: Home garage
levels.about: The garage at home: room for the race car and one more, if the family car lives outside.

levels.label: Rented shop bay
levels.about: A 1,500 sq ft bay in an industrial park: a lift, benches and room for three cars.

levels.label: Two-bay race shop
levels.about: 3,000 sq ft, two roll-up doors, a parts room and a tire room.

levels.label: Race shop & offices
levels.about: A 6,000 sq ft building with offices for sponsors to visit and room for a fleet.

space.note: Rent at the national industrial average, ~$8.76 per sq ft per year (2025, high); Mooresville race shops run $14 + $2.75 NNN (2025, medium).

fab.label: Fabrication

levels.label: Hand tools
levels.about: Wrenches and a grinder. Bent cars go to a chassis shop; you buy cars turnkey.

levels.label: Welder & tube bender
levels.about: A MIG welder, a tube notcher and bender: fix your own wrecks and assemble a car from a bare chassis (an amateur build gives a little away).

levels.label: Chassis jig & fixture table
levels.about: A surface plate and jig: frames come back straight and builds come out square. You can measure a used car before you buy it.

levels.label: Full fab shop
levels.about: TIG, a CNC tube bender, a sheet-metal brake and a body bench: your own builds are as good as the builders' and your chassis last longer.

fab.note: TIG welder $3,300-3,800, two-post lift $6,100-7,000 (retail, high). No public price for a chassis jig: EST.

engine.label: Engine room

levels.label: None
levels.about: Engines go to your builder for every freshen.

levels.label: Engine room
levels.about: A clean room, a parts washer, leak-down and valve-spring testers: you do the teardown and the builder does the machine work.

levels.label: Machine tools & flow bench
levels.about: Valve job, honing and a flow bench in house: cheaper freshens that last longer.

levels.label: Engine dyno cell
levels.about: Your own engine dyno: every engine is tuned before it goes in the car. (Sealed engines still go to the approved rebuilder.)

engine.note: An engine dyno cell all-in ~$70,000-80,000 (forum, low). Engine room and machine tools: EST.

setup.label: Setup tools

levels.label: Tape measure
levels.about: A tape measure, a bubble level and a notebook.

levels.label: Scales & alignment
levels.about: Wireless corner scales, a toe plate and caster/camber gauges: the car goes to the track the way you set it up.

levels.label: Shock dyno
levels.about: Build and match your own shocks instead of buying off the shelf.

levels.label: Data & simulation
levels.about: Data acquisition in the car, a setup program and a few seven-post shaker-rig days a year: the driver's feedback turns into speed.

setup.note: Wireless scales $1,450-2,700 and a setup rack $3,050-6,500 (retail, high); shock dynos $6,000-17,700 (2025, medium); driver-in-loop sim ~$12,000 a day (2017, medium). Seven-post rental rates: not found.

team._about: Owner mode facilities for a team-run team. Prices and upkeep are shares of the series' full-season cost per car (EST: no source gives these for teams below the Cup level).

rnd.label: Fabrication & R&D
rnd.about: Build your own chassis and bodies and develop parts between races: equipment grows faster.

engineering.label: Engineering
engineering.about: Simulator time, seven-post shaker rig and wind tunnel days: better race-day setups.

pit.label: Pit crew training
pit.about: A pit-stop practice facility, a strength coach and video review: faster, steadier stops.

transport.label: Transporters
transport.about: Newer haulers with full parts shops: sponsors like the look and the spares on board save races.

build._note: A bare chassis (frame, suspension mounts, body kit) costs about 80% of a turnkey roller; you supply the labour (EST).

market._note: Asking prices run 90-130% of a car's market value; selling your own car privately fetches about 80% of it (EST).
